nomenclature.etymology:
-
Bauhinia
: Commemorates the Swiss botanists Gaspard Bauhin (1560-1624) and his brother Jean (1541-1613), the twin leaflets of the leaf exemplify the two brothers.
-
Purpurea
: Refers to the purple colour of the flowers.

- Bauhinia : Commemorates the Swiss botanists Gaspard Bauhin (1560-1624) and his brother Jean (1541-1613), the twin leaflets of the leaf exemplify the two brothers.

stem_bark.text: The bark of Bauhinia purpurea is smooth or slightly fissured and scaly. The bark is ash-grey or brown coloured with longitudinal short dark marks. The heart-wood is brown, hard and durable.
stem_bark.text_html:
The bark of Bauhinia purpurea is smooth or slightly fissured and scaly. The bark is ash-grey or brown coloured with longitudinal short dark marks.
The heart-wood is brown, hard and durable.

seed.text: The seeds of Bauhinia purpurea are oblong or ovoid and flat, about 12-20 mm in diameter and 1-2 mm thick. Each pod contains 10 to 15 seeds. The seeds develop rapidly and trees in flower may already show numerous green pods.

fruit.text: The fruit of Bauhinia purpruea is a pod . This compressed and oblong pod is 15 to 35 cm long and 1 to 2.5 cm wide. The apex is horned and it is narrow at base. This pod is brownish with a tomentose stalk. The ripe dry fruits burst and scatter the seeds.

flower.text: The inflorescences of Bauhinia purpurea are terminal or axillary short and few-flowered racemes . The flowers are 6 to 10 cm across. The calyx is tubular and this tube is turbinate and coriaceous. It is erupted by the corolla along one side when the flower fully expanding. The calyx split into 2 valves, showing a division into 5 teeth (5-7 mm long). The lower tubular portion of the calyx is about 1.5 cm long and on the upper portion (or limb) is 3-3.5 cm long. The corolla is rose to pink and composed of 5 petals. The petals are entire, oblanceolate with a long claw (narrow at the base and apex obtuse). The petals are 4 to 7 cm long and 1 to 1.7 cm wide with a distinct central vein (midrib) and fine straight lateral veins. The fertile stamens are free, usually 3 (occasionally 4), slightly shorter than the petals. The rose-coloured and glabrous filaments are 3.5 to 4.5 cm long and the anthers are oblong and about 7 mm long and 2 mm wide. There are some filiform staminodes about 1 cm long. The ovary is about 1.5 cm, compressed and grooved. The pistil is long (5-6 cm long) and oblique. The pedicel is about 2 cm long. The flowers are fragrant. The buds are oblong or obovoid, with an apex obtuse, 3-4 cm long and 0.5-0.8 cm wide. These buds are strongly 5-ribbed, green coulored with white or light green longitudinal stripes.

leaf.text: The leaf of Bauhinia purpurea is wider than long (the blade is about 5-12 cm long and 6-14 cm wide). The leaf is formed of twin leaflets connate about half way.The leaf is deeply divided into two lobes sometimes overlapping and making the characteristic "camel foot" shape. The leaf is 11-13-nerved, thin and coriaceous with obtuse or slightly tapering apex and cordate base . The margin is entire. The upper side of the leaf is dark green coloured and the bottom is light-green. The petiole is 3 to 4 cm long with a triangular, hairy and 2-3 mm long stipule .

habit.text: Bauhinia purpurea is a middle-sized slender deciduous tree . It is a densely branched and foliaceous tree with a rounded crown attaining a height of 10 meters.
habit.text_html: Bauhinia purpurea is a middle-sized slender deciduous tree. It is a densely branched and foliaceous tree with a rounded crown attaining a height of 10 meters.

ecology.text: Bauhinia purpurea grows wild sporadically throughout India, particularly in the hill tracts. The tree is frequently cultivated for its showy flowers. It is a very popular garden tree and it is also planted on the roadsides. Bauhinia purpurea is a fast growing tree which grows in tropical and subtropical climates. It grows on various soils (relatively good soil conditions required) and it is found in different types of vegetation (from evergreen lowland rainforest to mountain forest, savannah or scrub and dry deciduous forest).

distribution.text: Bauhinia purpurea is native to south China (which includes Hong Kong) and south Asian countries (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Philippines, Malaysia...) The tree has been introduced to north and central America, Africa and Australia.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Bauhinia purpurea is pollinated by a wide variety of insects and sunbirds (in India). Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation. The seeds disperse from the pods and germinate on sites with favourable conditions : the ripe dry fruits burst and scatter the seeds.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

  • Seed dispersal :

    Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation.
    The seeds disperse from the pods and germinate on sites with favourable conditions : the ripe dry fruits burst and scatter the seeds.

culinary.text: The flower buds of Bauhinia purpurea are made into curries and pickles. The flower buds and young pods are tasty when they are cooked as vegetables. The tender leaves are eaten as vegetables and the seeds are eaten raw and roasted. Source : Edible Forest Foods of Tribals in South India, P. Rajyalakshmi

medicinal.text: The flowers of Bauhinia purpurea are laxative. A paste of the bark mixed with flowers and rice water is used to treat boils and abscesses. (T.N. Mukerji) The flower buds and flowers , fried in purified butter, are given to patients suffering from dysentery and an extract of stems is used internally and externally for fractured bones. (C.P. Khare) The bark of the stem is said to be a remedy for diarrhea (acts as an astringent). A decocoction of this astringent bark is also recommended to wash ulcers. (U.C. Dutt) The bark of the underground root is poisonous even in a small quantity. (Blatter & Millard) - Rasa (taste) : Kashaaya (astringent) - Guna (quality) : Ruksha (dry), Laghu (light) - Veerya (potency) : Sheeta (cooling) - Vipaaka (post-digestive taste) : Katu (pungent) - Karma (action) : By Ruksha (dry), Laghu (light) and Kashaaya (astringent) it is Kaphaghna (reduces Kapha). With Sheeta Veerya (cooling potency) it is Pittashaamaka (pacifies Pitta). Prabhaa (specificity) : Gandamaalaanaashana (reduces lymph node swelling) It is Vranashodhana (clean wounds) and Vranaropana (cure wounds). It is Kushthaghna (useful in skin diseases) and Shothahara (reduce inflammations and swellings). A decoction of the bark or leaves is used for Prakshaalana (cleansing) of Vrana (wounds) and Charmaroga (cutaneous diseases). A paste of the bark or leaves is applied on Gandamaalaa (lymph node swelling in the neck area). - Digestive system : Being Kashaaya (astringent), it is Stambhana (property to stop or block) and Krimighna (vermifugal). It is used in case of Atisaara (diarrhea), Pravaahikaa (dysentery - amoebic dysentery), Gudabhramsha (ano-rectal prolapse), Arsha (piles). Pushpa Gulakanda (flower jam) is given in Vibandha (constipation). - Circulatory system : Being Kashaaya (astringent) and Sheeta (cold), it is Raktastambhana (stops bleeding). It is used in Gandamaalaa (lymph node swelling), Lasikaagranthivriddhi (lymph node enlargement) and Shota (inflammatory swelling), Raktapitta (haemorrhage-bleeding). - Respiratory system : It is Kaasahara (heals cold and cough). - Urinary system : It is Mootrasangrahana (anuretic). It is used in Prameha (diabetes). - Reproductive system : Kashaaya (astringent) property helps in Aartavasraava (miscarriage). Used in Raktapradara (heavy menstrual bleeding). - Skin : It is Kushthaghna (reduces skin diseases). Bark, leaves and flowers - Bark powder : 3-6 gr - Decoction : 40-80 ml - Flower juice : 10-20 ml - On Dosha : Kaphapittaghna (alleviates Kapha and Pitta) - On Dhatu : Rakta, Meda (lymphadenitis), menorrhagia, haemorrhagic disorders - On Mala : Purisha (stool : stops diarrhea and prolapse)
medicinal.text_html:
The flowers of Bauhinia purpurea are laxative.

A paste of the bark mixed with flowers and rice water is used to treat boils and abscesses. (T.N. Mukerji)

The flower buds and flowers, fried in purified butter, are given to patients suffering from dysentery and an extract of stems is used internally and externally for fractured bones. (C.P. Khare)

The bark of the stem is said to be a remedy for diarrhea (acts as an astringent). A decocoction of this astringent bark is also recommended to wash ulcers. (U.C. Dutt)

The bark of the underground root is poisonous even in a small quantity. (Blatter & Millard)

Dravya Guna - Ayurvedic Pharmacology
Pancharasa | Essence of the plant

- Rasa (taste) : Kashaaya (astringent)
- Guna (quality) : Ruksha (dry), Laghu (light)
- Veerya (potency) : Sheeta (cooling)
- Vipaaka (post-digestive taste) : Katu (pungent)
- Karma (action) : By Ruksha (dry), Laghu (light) and Kashaaya (astringent) it is Kaphaghna (reduces Kapha). With Sheeta Veerya (cooling potency) it is Pittashaamaka (pacifies Pitta). Prabhaa (specificity) : Gandamaalaanaashana (reduces lymph node swelling)

External uses

It is Vranashodhana (clean wounds) and Vranaropana (cure wounds).
It is Kushthaghna (useful in skin diseases) and Shothahara (reduce inflammations and swellings).
A decoction of the bark or leaves is used for Prakshaalana (cleansing) of Vrana (wounds) and Charmaroga (cutaneous diseases).
A paste of the bark or leaves is applied on Gandamaalaa (lymph node swelling in the neck area).

Internal uses

- Digestive system : Being Kashaaya (astringent), it is Stambhana (property to stop or block) and Krimighna (vermifugal). It is used in case of Atisaara (diarrhea), Pravaahikaa (dysentery - amoebic dysentery), Gudabhramsha (ano-rectal prolapse), Arsha (piles). Pushpa Gulakanda (flower jam) is given in Vibandha (constipation).
- Circulatory system : Being Kashaaya (astringent) and Sheeta (cold), it is Raktastambhana (stops bleeding). It is used in Gandamaalaa (lymph node swelling), Lasikaagranthivriddhi (lymph node enlargement) and Shota (inflammatory swelling), Raktapitta (haemorrhage-bleeding).
- Respiratory system : It is Kaasahara (heals cold and cough).
- Urinary system : It is Mootrasangrahana (anuretic). It is used in Prameha (diabetes).
- Reproductive system : Kashaaya (astringent) property helps in Aartavasraava (miscarriage). Used in Raktapradara (heavy menstrual bleeding).
- Skin : It is Kushthaghna (reduces skin diseases).

Useful parts

Bark, leaves and flowers

Dosage

- Bark powder : 3-6 gr
- Decoction : 40-80 ml
- Flower juice : 10-20 ml

Toxicity

- On Dosha : Kaphapittaghna (alleviates Kapha and Pitta)
- On Dhatu : Rakta, Meda (lymphadenitis), menorrhagia, haemorrhagic disorders
- On Mala : Purisha (stool : stops diarrhea and prolapse)

Sources
- Sharma, P. V., 2001, Dravyaguna-Vijana. Chaukhambha Bharati Academy, Varanasi
- Vaidya V.M. Gogte, 2000, Ayurvedic Pharmacology and Therapeutic Uses of Medicinal Plants (Dravyagunavignyan). Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan

reforestation.text: This tree demands plenty of light; it should, therefore, be planted in open places away from buildings or from large shady trees. It is best to plant the seeds in good soil, about 20-25 cm apart. When the time for transplanting the seedlings comes, great care must be taken to see that the delicate rootlets are not damaged; the seedlings are rather sensitive to transplanting. ( R.S. Troup, Silviculture of Indian Trees ) Bauhinia purpurea can be sown without seed pretreatment but 12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    This tree demands plenty of light; it should, therefore, be planted in open places away from buildings or from large shady trees. It is best to plant the seeds in good soil, about 20-25 cm apart. When the time for transplanting the seedlings comes, great care must be taken to see that the delicate rootlets are not damaged; the seedlings are rather sensitive to transplanting. 
    (R.S. Troup, Silviculture of Indian Trees)

  • Seed treatments :

    Bauhinia purpurea can be sown without seed pretreatment but 12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
